title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Γ = SL(2,Z), and Γ^* is presumably GL(2,Z). Π = Γ^+[2] = Γ(2) = Ker(SL(2,Z) → SL(2,Z/2)). Since -1 ≡ I mod 2, the centre ±1 lies in Π. Π/±1 ≅ π_{0,3}, the free group on two generators: the fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, equivalently the level-2 modular curve. This gives the central extension (15): 1 → ±1 → Π → π_{0,3} → 1, together with its profinite version.

The page.
- Grothendieck has lifts l_0, l_1, l_∞ ∈ SL(2,Z) of the standard generators of π_{0,3}. They satisfy l_∞ l_1 l_0 = −1, which reflects the elliptic/Legendre normalisation.
- He sets λ_i := −l_i. Then λ_∞ λ_1 λ_0 = 1 (17), so l_i ↦ λ_i defines a homomorphism π_{0,3} → Π. It is a section of (15), so Π = Π_0 × {±1}, where Π_0 = ⟨λ_0, λ_1, λ_∞⟩ (18). The profinite statement is the same: Π^ = Π^_0 × {±1}.

Proposition.
- (a) Π_0 has index 2 in Π and is normal in Γ^* (in fact under all of GL(2,Z)).
- (b) Π^_0 has index 2 in Π^ and is normal in the large automorphism group M, equivalently stable under M/±1 ≅ M~_{0,3}. M is the group of automorphisms of the profinite completion of Γ^+ studied on the previous page, a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group attached to N~_{1,1} / M~_{0,3}.

Proof of (a). Use the explicit action of generators ρ (order 3), σ and τ (19):
- ρ cyclically permutes the λ_i.
- σ: λ_0 ↦ λ_1^{-1}, λ_1 ↦ λ_0^{-1}.
- τ inverts λ_0 and λ_1.
So ρ, σ, τ map Π_0 into itself, hence Π_0 is normalised by Γ (and Γ^*). Index 2 then follows from the direct-product decomposition.

Proof of (b) (next page). Write M = M(0)·Γ^. For u ∈ M(0):
- u(l_0) = l_0^μ with μ ∈ Ẑ^* odd, so u(λ_0) = λ_0^μ because (−1)^μ = −1.
- u(λ_1) = u(ρ(λ_0)) = (int(α)ρ)(λ_0^μ), which lies in Π^_0 since Π^_0 is normalised by Γ^.
Corollary: Π ≅ Π_0 × μ_2 and Π^ ≅ Π^_0 × μ_2, i.e. a canonical, M-stable free complement to the centre.

Concretely, with l_0 = [[1,2],[0,1]] and l_1 = [[1,0],[−2,1]], one gets Π_0 = Ker(χ_a χ_b χ_c), where χ_a(A) = a mod 4, χ_b = (−1)^{b/2} and χ_c = (−1)^{c/2}. Of the four complements to ±1 in Γ(2), this is the one fixed by the SL(2,Z/2) ≅ S_3 action. The more familiar complement ⟨[[1,2],[0,1]], [[1,0],[2,1]]⟩ (a ≡ 1 mod 4) is not normal in SL(2,Z). The aim is to have a canonical, Galois/GT-stable splitting of the profinite level-2 congruence group, to transport the M_{0,3} (GT-type) action into genus 1, i.e. to N_{1,1}.
errors: In (19), σ(λ_∞) is written as λ_1^{-1}λ_0^{-1}. Since λ_∞ = (λ_1λ_0)^{-1}, the given σ gives σ(λ_1λ_0) = λ_0^{-1}λ_1^{-1} = λ_∞, hence σ(λ_∞) = λ_∞^{-1} = λ_1λ_0. This is a harmless slip: the conclusion that Π_0 is σ-stable is unaffected.
"Index 2 is evident" really relies on −1 ∉ Π_0, i.e. on (16) being a section of the central extension. This is noted on the next page.

ideas.what: Γ(2) = {±1} × F_2, with an explicit free complement generated by the negatives of the standard lifts so that λ_∞λ_1λ_0 = 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Fricke–Klein era; standard in modular forms texts)

ideas.what: The symmetric complement Π_0 is normal in SL(2,Z) and even in GL(2,Z): it is the unique S_3-invariant complement among the four
ideas.modern_name: canonical SL(2,Z)-normal free complement in Γ(2) (index-12 normal free subgroup of SL(2,Z))

ideas.what: Profinite version: Π^_0 is stable under the large Teichmüller-type automorphism group M ≅ extension of M~_{0,3} by ±1, using u(λ_0) = λ_0^μ with μ odd
ideas.modern_name: GT (Grothendieck–Teichmüller) action on the profinite completion of SL(2,Z)/Γ(2) and genus-1 lifting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps; Hain–Matsumoto (GT and SL2(Z)^ / M_{1,1})

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly constructs an M-stable (GT-stable) canonical free complement to the centre ±1 in profinite Γ(2). This lets the genus-0 GT-type group act on profinite Γ(2) without the sign ambiguity, as early (unpublished) groundwork for the genus-1 / M_{1,1} lifting of GT later developed by Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and Hain–Matsumoto. The content is elementary and its genus-1 GT relevance is known in spirit, so it is mostly of historical interest.
missed.quote: Le sous-groupe Π̂_0 de Π̂ est d'indice 2 et il est distingué dans M — ou, ce qui revient au même, stable sous l'action de M/±1 ≃ M~_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own route from GT in genus 0 to SL2(Z)^ / M_{1,1}, and his sign-normalisation (λ_i = −l_i, a 'twisted Legendre' choice). This is relevant to the history of the GT action on M_{1,1}.

deep.surprise_reason: The splitting Γ(2) = ±1 × F_2 and the normality of the symmetric complement are elementary and classical. The profinite stability under Grothendieck's M is a natural lemma in his genus-1 extension of the GT program, an area later developed independently. It is a nice historical detail but not a hidden result.
transcription_corrections: Γ^* in Proposition a) and Γ in 'normalisé par ρ, σ, τ donc par Γ' are written with Grothendieck's script G (𝔊 / 𝔖), i.e. the same symbol as 𝔖^+ on the previous page, not plain Γ.
In (19), σ(λ_∞) = σ(λ_1λ_0)^{-1} = λ_1^{-1}λ_0^{-1} is what is written (crossed-out material precedes it). The mathematically correct value is λ_1λ_0.
In (16) the crossed-out symbol before λ_i is illegible; the 'dfn' over '=' is correctly read.
